title: Partial Views in Razor
description: Learn how to use partial views to break down complex Razor pages into reusable components.

blocks.text: A partial view is a Razor file that renders a standalone chunk of HTML. It does not have a layout page, it does not define sections, and it cannot be requested directly by a browser. Instead, it is rendered by another view, page, layout, or view component.

Partial views shine when you have a UI pattern that repeats across multiple pages. A product card, a comment thread, a sidebar widget, or a pagination control are all excellent candidates. By extracting them into partials, you write the markup once and reuse it everywhere.

blocks.title: Naming Convention
blocks.text: Partial view files conventionally start with an underscore, such as _ProductCard.cshtml. This signals to developers that the file is not meant to be accessed directly and is intended for reuse.

To create a partial view, add a new Razor View to the Views/Shared folder or to a feature-specific folder. The file should have a leading underscore in its name and contain only the markup for the reusable piece. The @model directive at the top defines the type the partial expects.

blocks.title: A Product Card Partial View
blocks.content: This partial renders a single product summary.
blocks.code:
@model Product
@Model.Name

@Model.ShortDescription

@Model.Price.ToString("C")

View Details

blocks.text: You can render a partial view from a view, layout, or view component using three approaches. The partial tag helper is the recommended approach because it reads naturally in HTML and supports model passing.

Html.PartialAsync returns an IHtmlContent that you can place anywhere in the markup. Html.RenderPartialAsync writes directly to the response stream, which is slightly faster but less flexible because it must be called inside a code block.

blocks.text: Passing a Model to a Partial

A partial view receives its data through the model parameter. If you do not pass a model explicitly, the partial inherits the same model as the parent view. This is convenient when the partial renders a small piece of the same data, but it can lead to tight coupling if overused.
For complex scenarios, pass a dedicated view model to the partial. This keeps the partial independent and easy to test in isolation.

blocks.title: Model Mismatch Risk
blocks.text: If the partial expects a Product but the parent passes a string or null, you will get a runtime error. Always verify that the model you pass matches the @model directive in the partial.

Partial views and view components both render reusable markup, but they have different strengths. A partial view is purely presentational: it receives data and renders it. A view component can run its own logic, call services, and prepare its own model before rendering.

cards.title: Partial View
cards.description: A reusable markup snippet that renders data provided by the parent.

cards.title: View Component
cards.description: A class plus view that encapsulates logic, data access, and rendering.

blocks.text: When you reference a partial by name, Razor searches for it in a specific order. It first looks in the same folder as the current view, then in the Shared folder, and finally in any locations configured through RazorViewEngineOptions. Using an underscore prefix and placing partials in Shared makes them easy to find.

terms.definition: A Razor file that renders a reusable HTML fragment without its own layout or page directive.
A tag helper that renders a partial view by name and optionally passes a model.
A helper method that renders a partial view and returns its HTML as IHtmlContent.
A more powerful alternative to partial views that includes logic and data access.
A class designed specifically to pass data to a view or partial view.

blocks.title: Exercise: Build a Comment Thread Partial
blocks.description: Create a reusable comment thread partial view for blog posts.
steps: Create a CommentViewModel class with AuthorName, Body, and CreatedAt properties.
Create a _CommentThread partial view in Views/Shared that takes an IEnumerable<CommentViewModel>.
Render each comment in an article or section with the author, date, and body.
Create a Blog Post page that supplies a list of comments to the partial.
Style the partial so it looks like a threaded conversation.
Refactor to pass a dedicated view model to the partial instead of using the parent model directly.
blocks.expectedOutcome: A reusable comment thread partial that can be dropped into any page that needs to display comments.

blocks.title: Summary
points: Partial views are reusable markup fragments without their own layout.
Use the partial tag helper, Html.PartialAsync, or Html.RenderPartialAsync to render them.
Partial views conventionally start with an underscore and live in the Shared folder.
Pass a model explicitly to keep the partial loosely coupled to its parent.
Choose partial views for presentational reuse and view components when logic or data fetching is needed.
blocks.takeaway: Partial views are the simplest and most effective way to eliminate duplicate markup. Used well, they keep your views short, focused, and easy to maintain.
